papers.title: Constraining Intergalactic Dust with Supernova Color Evolution: Current Constraints from DES and Forecasts for LSST and Roman
papers.abstract: Dust is an important systematic in precision Type Ia supernova (SN Ia) cosmology, and while dust in the Milky Way and SN host galaxies has been extensively studied, the impact of potential intergalactic dust is less well constrained. Using estimates from B. Ménard et al. (2010), we find that current intergalactic dust bounds could shift SN distance moduli by up to 0.02 mag at $z \gtrsim 1$ from simulations. However, we show dust models can be constrained independently by SN samples themselves via a specific predicted redshift-dependent evolution observed in SN colors. While current data from the Dark Energy Survey (DES) cannot distinguish between various amounts of intergalactic dust in our universe, we demonstrate that the Roman Space Telescope (Roman) will place a significant constraint on intergalactic dust models ($>$ 3$\sigma$). In contrast, the Rubin Observatory's Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), even with its unprecedented statistics, will only reach $\lesssim$ 2$\sigma$ significance on any given intergalactic dust prediction relative to no dust. We propagate multiple parameterizations of intergalactic dust through to cosmology. For LSST, we see a $\sim$60% reduction in the figure of merit (FoM) for $w$CDM and a $\sim$20% reduction for $w_0w_a$CDM, and for Roman, a $\sim$20% reduction in the FoM for $w$CDM and a $\sim$5% reduction for $w_0w_a$CDM. Utilizing Roman as an external constraint on dust for LSST results in a slightly improved FoM ($\sim$50% reduction) for $w$CDM for LSST. Finally, we show that intergalactic dust uncertainties decrease the FoM of the previous DES analysis (16.9% for $w$CDM and 8.1% for $w_0w_a$CDM) and that intergalactic dust cannot explain away recent hints for evolving dark energy.

papers.title: Resolving the Conformal Mode Problem with Einstein-Cartan Gravity
papers.abstract: We show that, when $\Lambda > 0$, the conformal factor problem is absent in first order Einstein-Cartan gravity in which the spin connection and tetrad are independent off-shell. At fixed connection, a conformal rescaling of the tetrad produces no conformal kinetic term so that the action is bounded from below. The original unbounded Einstein-Hilbert action, the Einstein-Hilbert action without the problematic conformal kinetic term and conformally invariant $R^{2}/\Lambda$ gravity arise as classical saddles of the Einstein-Cartan action with respect to the connection and conformal mode of the tetrad.

papers.title: CHEX-MATE: Probing the thermal$-$non-thermal connection in radio halo clusters with LoTSS-DR2
papers.abstract: The main baryonic component of galaxy clusters is in the form of a hot plasma observed in the X-rays. In addition, clusters host a non-thermal component (relativistic particles and magnetic fields) which is studied mainly via radio telescopes and is dynamically coupled to the thermal plasma. These two components evolve together within the system and are subject to both micro and macro-physical processes which can be traced only with deep and detailed observations. We present the first homogeneous spatially resolved radio--X-ray study of 18 radio halo clusters combining CHEX-MATE and the LOFAR Two metre Sky Survey DR2. Radio ($I_R$) and X-ray ($I_X$) surface brightness are clearly correlated (Spearman coefficient $r_s \ge 0.5$), following a typically sublinear $I_R-I_X$ relation ($67 \pm 5\%$ of the sample) that appears to be independent of other cluster properties, although a tentative trend with mass/redshift may be worth exploring with larger samples. When inspecting such a relation as a function of the radius, we observe a variety of behaviours, which suggest that the interplay between the thermal and non-thermal plasma components varies with radius. We find the averaged slope profile of dynamically disturbed clusters to be consistent with expectations from turbulent re-acceleration models where a constant ratio between cosmic-ray electron and thermal energy densities is assumed. Differently, less perturbed clusters require an increasing cosmic-ray-to-thermal energy ratio with radius. Finally, we show that radio halo surface-brightness profiles can be effectively rescaled using X-ray information and theoretical expectations. This procedure significantly reduces their scatter and reveals common underlying trends based on the cluster dynamics, resembling what is observed for the thermal ICM, and strengthening the idea of a strong interplay between these two plasma components.

papers.title: Quasinormal modes of black holes in astrophysical environments: Rainbow in the dark matter
papers.abstract: Matter around black holes affects the ringdown in two ways: through the background geometry and through the response of the matter itself. We compute axial and polar gravitational quasinormal modes of a black hole embedded in a relativistic Hernquist-type dark matter halo, following the fundamental mode and the first three overtones associated with the vacuum Schwarzschild spectrum. The polar sector couples metric and matter perturbations. At small halo compactness, both sectors follow the familiar gravitational redshift law. Most of the departure from the typical redshift at larger compactness is accounted for by the exact horizon lapse factor of the background. The remaining residual departure to this lapse is sector dependent. Axial and polar frequencies are split, with their splitting growing from the fundamental through the third overtone. At large halo compactness the split grows by an order of magnitude, while overtone-to-fundamental frequency ratios depart from a common rescaling. Within the adopted dark matter profile, the halo acts on the ringdown as a prism that disperses the gravitational spectrum, leaving a parity-dependent imprint that no common rescaling of the frequencies can reproduce. Parity-isospectrality is, thus, broken.

papers.title: Beyond the blur: Radial binning trumps stellar migration in resolved star formation histories
papers.abstract: Spatially resolved galaxy properties are routinely derived from integral-field spectroscopy and increasingly from multi-band photometry as a wealth of photometric data become available in large surveys like LSST/Rubin. Spatially resolved star formation histories (SFHs) offer a detailed view of galaxy growth and quenching by tracing the timing and location of star formation within a galaxy up to one billion years in the past. However, stellar migration between spaxels may strongly bias these reconstructions. Quantifying this bias remains challenging as few Milky-Way mass simulations fully resolve initial stellar dispersions or migration rates. We use the well-validated h277 Milky-Way-mass cosmological zoom simulation, which resolves both via explicitly tying star formation to the non-equilibrium abundance of H2, to assess the quality of specific star formation rates (sSFR) radial profiles inferred from resolved SFHs against actual values from stellar particle tracking. Across several evolutionary windows spanning a range of stellar activity stages from quiescent to star-bursting, we find that the adaptive radial binning imposed by S/N constraints in photometric SED fitting actually mitigates most of the blurring/mixing effects of stellar migration on inferred radial profiles up to lookback times of 1.5 Gyr. This allows for proper recovery of not only the average sSFR but also its radial slope, its relative changes in scatter across radial annuli and even approximate localization of low-z star-forming clumps. Only galaxies having undergone a major merger across the considered lookback time display discrepant, unreliable sSFR profiles, hence should not be considered for such reconstructions.

papers.title: Acoustic Priors from the Latest Cosmic Microwave Background Data
papers.abstract: We revisit the physics of the acoustic peaks and illustrate how early-Universe information in the cosmic microwave background (CMB) can be disentangled from late-time signatures imprinted by gravitational lensing and the integrated Sachs-Wolfe (ISW) effect. Applying this separation to Planck PR4, ACT DR6, and SPT-3G D1 temperature and polarization data combined with the joint lensing reconstruction, we update the model-independent constraints on the angular acoustic scale and the physical densities, $100\theta_*=1.04100\pm0.00021$, $\omega_{\rm b}=(2.2440\pm0.0099)\times10^{-2}$, and $\omega_{\rm bc}=0.1410\pm0.0011$. These constraints are consistent with the previous Planck PR4-only analysis and remain stable for extended late-time cosmologies beyond $\Lambda$CDM. Adding ACT DR6 to the combination favors a higher $\omega_{\rm b}$ and, through their correlation, a higher primordial tilt $n_{\rm s}$ than PR4 alone. The reconstructed lensing spectrum exceeds that of $\Lambda$CDM, with two features near $L\simeq50$ and $L\sim10^3$, and the excess is reduced when WMAP replaces the Planck primary spectra. Marginalizing over the lensing-induced peak smoothing, rather than tying it to the late-time model, lowers the preference of the CMB and DESI DR2 baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) for $w_0w_a$CDM over $\Lambda$CDM from $3.0\sigma$ to $1.9\sigma$, or from $3.2\sigma$ to $2.4\sigma$ when Union3.1 supernovae are added. We further use the acoustic prior to predict BAO distances from CMB data alone under several late-time expansion histories, testing their consistency with DESI measurements assuming standard pre-recombination physics.

papers.title: Hamiltonian approach to isospectrality in nonrotating black holes
papers.abstract: In this work, we revisit the isospectrality of black hole perturbations from a Hamiltonian perspective. For a nonrotating, uncharged system, we present a convenient canonical description of the background degrees of freedom that facilitates comparison with the usual Lagrangian formulation. This allows us to identify phase-space counterparts of the superpotential and the algebraically special modes and show that they satisfy the expected isospectral relations, at least on shell or off shell modulo some subtle lapse redefinitions. Finally, we investigate the extent to which these results persist in theories that effectively modify general relativity. In this setting, we formally quantify the corresponding deviations from the classical relations and the associated potential violations of isospectrality to first order in the modifications.

papers.title: Modular fluctuation relations on local causal horizons
papers.abstract: Local causal horizons provide a setting for studying horizon thermodynamics in the neighborhood of any regular spacetime point. Here, we investigate this description beyond mean energy and entropy balances by studying fluctuations of boost-energy transfer induced by unitary perturbations of the horizon reference state. Using the modular structure of the horizon algebra and a thermal reference state, we construct an energy transfer probability measure and derive integral and detailed fluctuation relations with the mean entropy production being expressed in terms of the Araki relative entropy. The formulation accommodates type-III algebras without introducing a reduced density matrix and can be extended to global bifurcate Killing horizons admitting the required thermal reference state. For coherent scalar-field perturbations, we obtain a closed form for the characteristic function, identify the mean transfer with the excess boost-energy flux, and derive a thermodynamic uncertainty relation bounding the variance in terms of the mean transfer. We then explore the geometric implications by postulating a stochastic horizon entropy--area correspondence that associates an area change with each counted energy transfer. Under this additional hypothesis, we obtain fluctuation relations for area changes and an area change uncertainty bound for coherent perturbations.

papers.title: Low-latency gravitational wave alert infrastructure and new data products for multi-messenger astronomy during LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA's fourth observing run
papers.abstract: Multi-messenger investigations of compact object mergers, such as binary neutron star and neutron star-black hole systems, remain among the most dynamic frontiers of modern astronomy. During the fourth observing run of Advanced LIGO, Advanced Virgo, and KAGRA, the search for joint electromagnetic and neutrino counterparts to gravitational-wave signals continued using public, semi-automated data products distributed in near real-time. The sky localizations and preliminary source characterizations provided by these alerts helped guide multiple rapid follow-up observations to candidate gravitational-wave events. During this run, the low-latency search parameter space was expanded to include the sub-solar mass regime and associated public data products were developed. Further, chirp mass estimates of the binary merger system were introduced as a new public data product and distributed to enable follow-up searches to concentrate their resources on the most promising transients. In order to streamline the implementation of new searches and data products, a mock data challenge, known as the Low-Latency Production Integration Challenge (LLPIC), was used as a replay of a simulated population of gravitational-wave sources to optimize and profile the software infrastructure and scientific deliverables. In this paper we describe these new public data products, their performance and the result of end-to-end testing of the low-latency infrastructure with the LLPIC.

papers.title: A Variability Metric Pipeline for AGN studies
papers.abstract: Variability in active galactic nuclei (AGNs) is remarkably diverse, spanning multiple timescales, wavelengths, and physical processes. Variability probes accretion physics and the interplay between supermassive black holes and their surroundings. Building on early case studies, the field has shifted toward population-level analyses of increasingly large datasets, making scalable techniques crucial for upcoming time-domain surveys. We developed a Python-based pipeline to analyze AGN light curves using variability metrics and applied it to 14,061 nearby AGNs ($z\lesssim 0.09$) observed with ZTF. We examined metric distributions and correlations. Amplitude-based metrics (e.g., $F_{\rm var}$) help identify major flares but are sensitive to single deviant epochs. Temporal metrics such as $\eta$ provide a complementary check. Comparison with WISE infrared photometry suggests that $\eta$ traces the strength of AGN activity. Most Type~I and Type~II AGNs in our sample exhibit similar variability patterns based on these metrics. This overlap may partly reflect misclassifications that targeted spectroscopic follow-up could help resolve. To identify subsets of AGNs with distinctive variability, we used UMAP to group sources with similar metric values. The resulting embedding shows a region enriched in high-amplitude variables, including a subset with long-term flux trends. We find evidence that extremely variable quasars and changing-look AGNs may populate this region, which can help prioritize sources for follow-up. Our pipeline offers a scalable, survey-agnostic framework suitable for application to Vera C. Rubin Observatory's LSST and other ongoing and upcoming photometric surveys.

papers.title: No Cluster Left Behind I: Joint Mass Calibration for Dark Energy Survey and South Pole Telescope Clusters
papers.abstract: Multiwavelength observations of galaxy clusters are among the most promising probes of the growth of structure and dark energy. Optically identified clusters have a high number density and can thus probe the halo mass function well into the group regime, but their weak-lensing mass calibration suffers from a selection bias induced by line-of-sight projection effects. Clusters detected via their intracluster medium (ICM) -- through X-ray emission or the thermal Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect (SZe) -- are less affected by such selection biases, but current survey sensitivity restricts ICM-selected samples to high-mass systems. Previous multiwavelength analyses tend to limit to clusters with millimeter detections and thus to the high-mass population. In this paper, we propose a flexible modeling framework in which all clusters from multiwavelength surveys can be combined and modeled, even if they are detected in only one survey. As a pilot study, we jointly model richness and lensing of clusters from the Dark Energy Survey and the SZe signal from the South Pole Telescope. This approach yields precise cluster mass calibration while self-consistently constraining optical selection biases. We have found a $\sim$20% bias in the large-scale lensing signal of clusters selected by richness, and a bias ranging from $\sim-20$% at low richness to zero at high richness for clusters selected by both richness and SZe. Compared to current approaches, this framework is highly scalable and readily extensible, paving the way for the full utilization of multiwavelength cluster data in next-generation surveys.

papers.title: Inference of Cosmic Dawn and Reionization Parameters from the 21 cm Global Spectrum Measurement of the DSL Mission
papers.abstract: The 21 cm global spectrum is an important observable for cosmic dawn and epoch of reionization. The Discovering the Sky at the Longest Wavelengths mission (DSL, also known as Hongmeng), will measure the 21 cm global spectrum from the lunar orbit, thus avoiding the systematic effects common in ground based experiments, potentially producing the most accurate measurement to date. In this paper, we present a Bayesian inference framework, and investigate the constraints that can be placed on the cosmic dawn and reionization model parameters, either from the 21 cm global spectrum data alone, or from its combination with 21\,cm spatial power-spectrum data. For the global spectrum data, we assume a residual error equivalent to the thermal noise of a total observation of 30, 300, or 3000 orbit cycles of DSL. For the power spectrum, we adopt representative forecasts for HERA or SKA-Low. We find that there is generally a degeneracy between the foreground and the 21 cm global signal, and one has to make some restrictions on the form of either the foreground or the 21 cm global spectrum to break this degeneracy. Using the physically motivated emulator 21cmEMU, we generate the 21 cm global spectrum and power spectrum under a common astrophysical parameterization, while marginalizing over the foreground parameters. We derive constraints for two representative models, with their global spectrum absorption minimum at 105 and 94 MHz respectively. With only the global spectrum data, there remains much degeneracy in the astrophysical parameters. We find that the spatial power spectrum is highly complementary to the global spectrum, which can break the degeneracy and tighten up the constraints significantly.

papers.title: Environmental resonances in extreme-mass-ratio inspirals within boson clouds
papers.abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) offer a promising probe of matter environments around massive black holes through gravitational-wave (GW) observations. We investigate orbital resonances induced by conservative gravitational perturbations from such environments. Combining a multiparameter expansion with the action-angle formalism, we derive a general resonance condition for generic bound Kerr orbits. Applying this framework to ultralight scalar clouds formed through black hole superradiance, we show that orbital resonances can arise from a single-mode cloud without requiring transitions between cloud modes. Our analysis demonstrates that these resonances can lead to significant GW dephasing, providing a new avenue for probing boson clouds through GWs and highlighting the importance of including environmental resonances in accurate EMRI waveform modeling.

papers.title: JWST Reveals Contrast Overdensities around Two ALMA-CRISTAL Galaxies at $z\sim5.2$
papers.abstract: The distribution of stellar mass between massive galaxies and their companions traces how galaxy assembly proceeds within early large-scale structure. We investigate the environments of two galaxies from the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) CRISTAL survey: CRISTAL-19 (C19; $z=5.235$) and CRISTAL-21 (C21; $z=5.256$), using F444W slitless spectroscopy from the Near-Infrared Camera (NIRCam) on the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) in COSMOS-3D. A friends-of-friends analysis of H$\alpha$ emitters identifies two distinct overdense nodes separated by approximately 25 comoving Mpc. Although C21 is the more massive galaxy, C19 has the more massive, actively star-forming companions. The companion populations around C19 and C21 have median stellar masses of $\log(M_\star/M_\odot)=9.43$ and 8.82 and median dust-corrected H$\alpha$ star formation rates of 31 and $16~M_\odot~\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, respectively. Their star formation rate contrast largely reflects the difference in companion masses. C19 contains only $4.5^{+0.9}_{-0.7}\%$ of the combined measured stellar mass of itself and its selected companions; the corresponding fraction for C21 is $39^{+5}_{-5}\%$. Thus, stellar mass remains more widely distributed among galaxies around C19, whereas a larger share resides in C21. Resolved interacting companions around C19 and [C II] kinematics consistent with a late-stage merger in C21 support this contrast in assembly state. These findings support the phase-dependent picture of Zou et al. (2026), in which the surrounding star-forming population changes as interactions and mergers build up a massive galaxy.

papers.title: Towards three-dimensional dark matter mapping in the extended solar neighbourhood with Gaia Data Release 3 and deep learning
papers.abstract: We investigate a method for inferring the local dark matter (DM) density in the solar neighbourhood using a deep learning framework that learns the mapping between stellar kinematics and the underlying DM density field from cosmological simulations. To this end, we construct a training set from 7 Milky Way-like galaxies in the FIRE-2 simulation suite. We use three-dimensional stellar kinematic components, consisting of the tangential velocities along the right ascension and declination directions ($v_{\alpha*}$ and $v_{\delta}$) derived from parallaxes and proper motions, together with radial velocity, as input features to predict the three-dimensional DM density field. Two distinct architectures, VNet (arXiv:1606.04797) and ViT-VNet (arXiv:2205.08534), are trained on identical datasets. Both models reproduce the large-scale DM density gradient, whereas small-scale fluctuations are systematically smoothed. Applying the trained models to Gaia DR3 data yields our best estimates of the local DM density: $0.80^{+0.10}_{-0.10}$ and $1.12^{+0.15}_{-0.13}$ GeV cm$^{-3}$ from VNet and ViT-VNet, respectively. The quoted uncertainties reflect the inference scatter across the training set. We further examine systematics from model dependence and the simulation-Gaia domain mismatch, providing an initial step towards a framework for reconstructing local DM maps from future multi-epoch astrometric measurements, including those expected from Gaia DR4.

papers.title: AT2024dky as an Off-nuclear Tidal Disruption Event Candidate
papers.abstract: Through a retrospective search for tidal disruption events (TDEs) in the ZTF archives agnostic to their location within their host galaxies, we identify AT2024dky/ZTF24aagksvd as a promising off-nuclear TDE candidate. At $z=0.0592$, it lies at a projected offset of $3.72^{\prime\prime}$ (4.26 kpc) from the center of a massive ($M_{\rm gal}\sim10^{11}\,M_\odot$), quiescent galaxy. We present early-time ZTF and ATLAS optical photometry and late-time follow-up observations with Keck-I/LRIS, VLA, EP, and Chandra. With $M_{g,\rm peak}=-18.50$ mag, AT2024dky exhibits persistently blue color ($g-r\sim-0.1$ mag) through 80 d after peak. At $\delta t=858$ d, Keck reveals $M_{u'}=-13.07\pm0.09$ mag and $M_R > -14.15$ mag. At $\delta t=866$ d, VLA detects the transient at $\nu L_{\nu,10\,\rm GHz}=(1.26\pm0.17)\times10^{38}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$. The combination of early photometric evolution, detected late-time radio and UV emission strongly favor a TDE interpretation. The properties of its host galaxy also bear remarkable similarities to the parent galaxies of known off-nuclear TDEs. Based on the low values of peak-time and late-time UV/optical luminosities, we favor a black hole mass of $\sim 10^5$--$10^6 M_\odot$. Together, these observations strongly favor an off-nuclear TDE.

papers.title: Less massive black holes in faint hosts: SED fitting of Little Red Dots within the Black Hole Star scenario
papers.abstract: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has revealed a population of compact sources known as ``little red dots'' (LRDs), characterized by a distinctive V-shaped spectral energy distribution (SED) from UV to optical wavelengths. The physical nature of these sources remains debated. The ``black hole star'' (BH*) scenario, wherein a super-Eddington accreting black hole is embedded in a dense gaseous envelope, has been proposed to explain them. We assemble a sample of 22 LRDs at $4.0 \lesssim z \lesssim 9.5$ from the ASTRODEEP-JWST database. We construct a composite ``host galaxy + BH*'' model using the \texttt{Cloudy} photoionization code, and perform SED fitting with \textsc{BayeSED3}. Our modeling reproduces the observed V-shaped features: the UV continuum blueward of the Balmer break is well reproduced by stellar emission within this decomposition, while the optical regime is dominated by the BH* component. Our fits reveal that LRDs are black holes hosted by faint, low-mass galaxies with median stellar and black hole masses of $M_* = 10^{8.7}\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\rm BH} = 10^{6.4}\,M_\odot$, respectively. These black holes are moderately overmassive relative to local scaling relations but less extreme than broad-line estimates. The median bolometric luminosity $L_{\rm BH^*} \sim 10^{44.9}\,\rm erg\,s^{-1}$ mitigates the reported number density tension from 1--2 orders of magnitude to a factor of a few. The host galaxies lie near the high-redshift star-forming main sequence, and stellar extinction correlates positively with star formation rate (SFR). The BH* scenario provides a self-consistent paradigm for LRDs, offering insights into the rapid growth of supermassive black hole seeds and their co-evolution with host galaxies during the cosmic dawn.

papers.title: Cosmographic Analysis of Gravitational Baryogenesis in Running-$G$ Cosmology
papers.abstract: Gravitational baryogenesis produces a baryon asymmetry through the coupling of the baryon current to the derivative of the Ricci scalar, so its yield is set by the expansion history around decoupling. We study this mechanism in cosmology with a running Newton coupling of the asymptotic-safety type. Writing the Ricci scalar and its derivative through the Hubble rate, the deceleration parameter $q$ and the jerk $j$, we show that the yield is proportional to the kernel $K=2+q-j$, which vanishes for radiation in general relativity, and to a power of an enhancement factor measuring how strongly the running coupling accelerates the expansion at decoupling. We treat hybrid, intermediate, logamediate, emergent, bouncing and little-rip scale factors and determine where the observed asymmetry is reproduced for the $J^\mu\partial_\mu R$ and $J^\mu\partial_\mu R^2$ couplings; a table compares the six cases.

papers.title: Directional Statistics of Synchrotron Polarization in Mixed Emitting and Faraday-Rotating Turbulence
papers.abstract: Polarization directions provide a sensitive probe of Faraday rotation without weighting the signal by polarized brightness. We develop their spatial statistics for a turbulent volume in which synchrotron emission and Faraday rotation coexist. For independent, zero-mean Gaussian polarized emissivity, we derive an exact relation for the directional correlation. We derive strong stochastic coherence-depth scalings, including an additional interval for steep Faraday-density spectra, and distinguish them from the conditions needed to infer directional spectral slopes. We also quantify the weak-rotation response of a coherent uniform emitter and demonstrate that the scalings of the normalized tangential polarization gradient follow directly from the direction spectrum. A combined use of the techniques, including those introduced earlier in Lazarian & Pogosyan (2016), provides a way for detailed study of astrophysical turbulence.

papers.title: Multiwavelength Analysis of the Merging Cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8: A Three-way Merger in Disguise?
papers.abstract: We identify the galaxy cluster RM J121917.6+505432.8 as a candidate bimodal merging cluster due to its optical properties listed in the redMaPPer cluster catalog. To confirm the cluster's merging state and reveal its dark matter halo and intracluster medium (ICM) morphologies, we conducted a multiwavelength follow-up campaign encompassing HST/ACS optical observations, XMM-Newton X-ray imaging, and Keck/Deimos multislit spectroscopy. The weak lensing mass reconstruction performed with the HST images shows two resolved peaks whose positions coincide with the two brightest cluster galaxies. The ICM morphology is consistent with a post-pericenter merger, with significant asymmetry in X-ray flux between subclusters. Our Keck/Deimos redshift measurements reveal a relative velocity $\Delta v_{\mathrm{LOS}} = 480$ km s$^{-1}$ between eastern and western subclusters. The eastern, more massive subcluster, however, exhibits a highly elongated shape, suggesting either a dark matter halo of considerable eccentricity or the presence of a third, unresolved halo, eliciting the question of whether RMJ1219 is truly binary or a three-way merger. To investigate these hypotheses, we fit the weak lensing shear data using four different combinations of spherical and elliptical NFW halo models and provide an estimate of the mass and concentration of each subhalo. Although the best fit is achieved with a three-halo model, the data are insufficient to determine whether the introduction of extra parameters is statistically justified.

papers.title: The role of hierarchy in Galactic molecular clouds
papers.abstract: To probe the role of hierarchical gas structures in massive star formation, we statistically analyzed 13 Galactic massive star-forming regions using FUGIN CO survey data. Applying a non-binary dendrogram to the position-position-velocity data, we classified the extracted structures into trunks, internal leaves (the densest substructures within trunks), and isolated structures, and compared their properties with an analysis of variance controlling for regional differences. In representative regions, the trunks correspond to morphologies such as filaments and hub-filament systems, or to kinematic signatures of structure-forming events such as cloud-cloud collisions. Across the sample, the trunks are extended, massive, and strongly bound reservoirs, while the leaves are significantly more massive, denser, and more tightly bound than isolated structures of similar spatial scale. Using YSOs and Hi-GAL clumps, we find that the leaves have a lower low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures, whereas their clump formation efficiency is comparable. At a fixed gas mass, the leaves show no higher low-mass star formation efficiency than isolated structures but convert a larger fraction of their gas into dense clumps. We interpret these contrasts, together with inward gas motions in the position-velocity diagrams, as indicating that the deep potential of the trunks sustains continuous accretion onto the leaves and promotes mutual interactions among them. These processes may raise the characteristic fragmentation mass, as theoretically expected for a dynamically accreting medium, so that a larger fraction of the gas forms massive clumps without a corresponding increase in low-mass star formation. Our single-epoch data constrain only these structural contrasts, but indicate that the gas available for massive star formation is organized on scales larger than a single core.

papers.title: An Electromagnetic Ergoregion Limits the Reconnection-Driven Penrose Process
papers.abstract: Magnetic reconnection taps black-hole rotational energy via negative-energy ejecta, but field geometry itself can forbid such ejection inside the spacetime ergoregion. We identify a covariant electromagnetic (EM) ergoregion for general degenerate, magnetically dominated fields in stationary spacetimes. Outside the EM ergoregion, even ultrarelativistic field-guided ejecta cannot attain negative Killing energy. For Alfvénic reconnection outflows, the magnetization threshold scales inversely with the transverse distance to the EM ergosurface. The mass-loaded Kerr model places the EM ergosurface at about 75% of the radial interval from the horizon to the spacetime ergosurface, close to the time-averaged boundary inferred from a dynamical simulation. Together, these results show that field geometry determines where negative-energy ejection is possible, while magnetization sets the threshold for realizing it.

papers.title: Kiselev black hole from semiclassical gravity with conformal anomaly
papers.abstract: Investigating black hole physics in semi-classical gravitational theory is an interesting and important direction. When the backreaction of the conformal anomaly-induced effective stress-energy tensor is taken into account, the black hole spacetime can be largely altered which changes many properties of the black hole. In this work, rather than restricting our attention to the type-A anomaly, we incorporate the type-B anomaly and investigate how it modifies the spacetime structure obtained when only the type-A anomaly is considered. We find that for a specific relation between the central charges and the cosmological constant, the semiclassical Einstein equations can be solved analytically, yielding a metric that takes the exact form of the Kiselev black hole. After deriving the solution, we further discuss the properties of this new black hole solutions. Our work serves as an essential stepping stone for studying black hole geometries under the full conformal anomaly.

papers.title: Halo spin-axis correlations in IllustrisTNG: Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping, baryonic effects, and redshift-space distortions
papers.abstract: We investigate correlations of halo and stellar spin axes in the TNG300 volume of the IllustrisTNG simulations and compare them with a model based on linear tidal torque theory (LTTT). Dark matter (DM) halo spin axes at $z = 0$ exhibit positive correlations as a function of Lagrangian pair separation. The LTTT-based model describes their separation dependence well, with weak variation in the fitted amplitude across mass thresholds. A Lagrangian-to-Eulerian separation mapping based on the conditional distributions of initial separations at fixed present-day separation, measured directly from the simulations, allows the model to reproduce the overall trends in both real and redshift space without additional fitting. The hydrodynamic and DM-only runs generally show similar DM halo spin-axis correlations, although the DM-only run exhibits a steeper rise at small real-space separations. In the hydrodynamic run, stellar spin-axis correlations are consistent with the same Lagrangian form as their DM halo counterparts, but with approximately 60% of the DM correlation amplitudes. Positive stellar correlations persist in both real and redshift space, and the mapped model captures their separation dependence. Initial spin-axis correlations of protohalos are substantially stronger than their present-day counterparts at the same Lagrangian separations, consistent with subsequent nonlinear spin evolution weakening these correlations. These results suggest that present-day halo and stellar spin-axis correlations retain signatures of the initial tidal field and that their general behavior can be understood through LTTT-based modeling combined with pair-separation mapping.

papers.title: Radio Emission From Low-redshift Little Red Dots
papers.abstract: High-redshift Little Red Dots (LRDs) are radio faint in existing survey and deep-field samples. Nearby LRD analogues allow the radio emission and spectra of individual sources to be measured, which is not possible at $z\sim6$. Our sample comprises 44 low-redshift LRDs ($0.101 \leq z \leq 0.882$) . Eight objects are radio-detected: five at 144\,MHz with LoTSS, six at 3\,GHz with VLASS at $\geq3\sigma$, and J1047 through its published VLA data. The rest-frame 144\,MHz luminosities of the LoTSS detections span $1.8\times10^{30}$ to $3.6\times10^{31}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}\,Hz^{-1}}$. The LoTSS--VLASS spectral indices range from $-0.27\pm0.04$ (J2048) to $-0.78\pm0.11$ (J1200). J1051 lacks 144\,MHz coverage and has $\alpha_{0.9 \rm GHz}^{\rm 3 GHz} \simeq-0.93$. J1047 has a clear deficit at 144 MHz relative to its optically thin GHz spectrum, consistent with a turnover whose position and physical mechanism are not uniquely constrained by the archival data. The higher detection fraction among the Green Pea sample largely reflects their lower redshift: in this subsample LoTSS reaches luminosities roughly an order of magnitude fainter than in the more distant DESI gold sample. If their escaping spectra and radio luminosities are held fixed and extrapolated as power laws, the five LoTSS detections would have observed-frame 144 MHz flux densities of $\sim0.7$--$32\,\mu\mathrm{Jy}$. Low-redshift LRDs span more than an order of magnitude in radio luminosity among the detections, and more than two orders of magnitude when the J1047 upper limit is included. They also show several distinct spectral shapes, so the optically defined LRD class encompasses diverse radio properties. Current detection statistics are strongly shaped by redshift and survey sensitivity. The source-by-source luminosity limits provide a reference for interpreting future LRD samples.

papers.title: Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU): the fraction of radio-detected quasi-stellar objects at high redshift
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to use the Evolutionary Map of the Universe (EMU) to assess the fraction of high-z quasi-stellar objects (QSOs) that are radio-emitting at ~0.2 mJy/beam level and to establish if the radio emission is mainly produced by relativistic jets. A sample of 808 type1 QSOs in the redshift range 4<z<9 and covering the sky area currently observed by EMU was compiled from the literature and the SDSS spectroscopic database and cross-matched with EMU source catalogue. In total, 124 high-z QSOs are detected by EMU, corresponding to 15% of the sample. The large majority (70%) of the QSOs radio detected by EMU are reported in the radio for the first time. We use this sample to establish the detection rate at different optical magnitudes. We show that the fraction of radio-loud (R>10) high-z QSOs is about 8% while the fraction of radio detections is a strong function of the optical magnitude and reaches values of ~35% when only the optically brightest (mag~18) QSOs are considered. Since all the radio detected QSOs, including those classified as radio-quiet (R<10), exhibit radio powers ranging from 5x10^24 to 5x10^27 W Hz^-1 at 5 GHz, we argue that they could all host a relativistic jet and that orientation could be one of the main causes of the different values of radio-loudness observed in the sample. To support this hypothesis, we show that the number of high-z QSOs detected by EMU is fully consistent with the predictions based on the beaming model, using as reference the high-z blazars discovered at higher radio flux densities. The results presented here suggest that relativistic jets could have been very common in the early Universe representing up to ~35% of the luminous (L_1450A>10^46 erg s^-1) QSO population. Future observations with SKAO will be instrumental to unambiguously confirm the jetted nature of the QSOs currently detected by EMU.

papers.title: The type-D accelerating Taub-NUT spacetime: construction, geometry and physical properties
papers.abstract: We investigate the geometry and physical properties of the vacuum type-D accelerating Taub--NUT spacetime in the sector with vanishing Kerr rotation. We recover its normalized metric from the Plebański--Demiański family and a dressed finite binary, tracking the horizon Killing directions through the large-companion limit. The black-hole and acceleration horizons have distinct projective Killing generators, and their intrinsic horizon geometry yields a relation between polar Gaussian curvatures and cone angles that differs from that of the type-I accelerating Taub--NUT solution without requiring a matching of acceleration parameters. We establish separability of the type-D null Hamilton--Jacobi equation and construct an unwrapped radial conformal atlas with four simple-horizon extensions and five angular conformal diagrams. We also examine axial identifications and chronology-violating regions. The resulting geometrical and dynamical distinctions clarify how the two accelerating NUT families differ despite sharing their nonaccelerating and zero-NUT limits; the radial atlas is not claimed to be a unique maximal four-dimensional extension.

papers.title: Lorentz charges for Lovelock gravity
papers.abstract: In this paper, we construct the charges associated with the residual local Lorentz transformations on a black hole horizon in the Lovelock class of theories of gravity. The horizons is assumed to be non- expanding horizons, \emph{i.e} a null hypersurface for which the expansion corresponding to the null generator vanish. Naturally, these hypersurfaces preserve only a subgroup of the full Lorentz group of the bulk, and the residual symmetries correspond to the little group which stabilizes the horizon null generator. We show that on the horizon, the Hamiltonian charge corresponding to the residual local Lorentz boost is the Wald entropy.

papers.title: Bar Kinematics in Paired and Isolated Galaxies: Slow Bars Are More Likely Found in Paired Galaxies
papers.abstract: Bars are common structures in disk galaxies that can strongly influence the evolution of their hosts. Simulations predict that bars formed through tidal interactions tend to rotate slower than bars formed in isolation. We test this prediction observationally by studying the kinematics of 314 bars in galaxies between $0.016<z<0.130$. We use estimates of the bar pattern speed ($\Omega_p$) and the rotation rate ($\mathcal{R}$) obtained from four studies using IFU data from the MaNGA survey. We cross-match the host galaxies of the bars to the Galaxy Zoo DESI catalogue in order to study their environment and classify each galaxy as paired or isolated. We find that bars that are slower in terms of $\mathcal{R}$ are more likely to be found in paired galaxies. The fraction of bars in paired galaxies increases from $5^{+6}_{-2}\%$ for $0<\mathcal{R}<1.0$ to $31^{+15}_{-9}\%$ for $3.0<\mathcal{R}<4.0$. Our results also suggest a possible difference in the distribution of $\mathcal{R}$ between paired (mean $\mathcal{R}=2.1 \pm 0.2$) and isolated (mean $\mathcal{R}=1.75 \pm 0.07$) galaxies (p-value=0.037; 2.09$\sigma$). On the other hand, our analysis reveals no noticeable trend between the fraction of paired galaxies and the bar pattern speed, which indicates that the pattern speed is not correlated with the likelihood of a galaxy being paired. We also find no difference in the distribution of $\Omega_p$ between paired and isolated galaxies (p-value$>$0.250; $<$1.15$\sigma$).

papers.title: Small-scale priors for large-scale cosmology: the case of $b_ϕ$
papers.abstract: Perturbative descriptions of galaxy clustering introduce free bias parameters that capture the complex physics of galaxy formation. Local primordial non-Gaussianity (PNG), parametrized by $f_{NL}$, induces a scale-dependent contribution to the galaxy bias that is proportional to $f_{NL} b_\phi$, where $b_\phi$ quantifies how galaxy formation responds to PNG. Accurately determining $b_{\phi}$ is therefore essential for robust constraints on $f_{NL}$. Current analyses usually adopt a modified universal relation, $b_\phi = 2\delta_c(b_1-p)$, with $p$ calibrated to simulations. This relies on the accuracy of the simulated galaxy-formation model and ignores the uncertainty on $b_\phi$, potentially biasing $f_{NL}$ constraints. We investigate whether $b_\phi$ can be constrained from small-scale galaxy clustering using a flexible empirical galaxy-formation model. We fit an extended Subhalo Abundance Matching (SHAMe) model to small-scale clustering measurements and combine it with dark-matter-only separate-universe simulations to infer a posterior on $b_\phi$. We validate the method using IllustrisTNG hydrodynamical separate-universe simulations. Without calibration on hydrodynamical simulations, SHAMe predicts $b_\phi$ with a median error of 10%, compared with 38% for a fixed halo occupation distribution (HOD) that neglects the occupation response to $\phi$, and 23% for the universality relation. The residual error is dominated by central galaxies near the selection threshold and persists when using the true stellar-mass assignment conditioned on the same subhalo properties. Small-scale clustering combined with a subhalo-based empirical model predicts most of galaxy-abundance response to local PNG. The remainder depends on galaxy-formation physics and should enter $b_\phi$ priors as a theoretical uncertainty. This provides a route to data-informed priors on bias parameters.

papers.title: Sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in spherical symmetry
papers.abstract: We establish sharp decay and regularity thresholds for Minkowski stability in the spherically symmetric Einstein--scalar field system. For small smooth characteristic data measured in weighted derivative seminorms, we prove global stability at borderline decay and half-derivative regularity of the initial data. The resulting developments remain uniformly close to Minkowski spacetime and are future causally geodesically complete. Both thresholds are sharp: below either the decay or regularity threshold, we construct arbitrarily small smooth, initially untrapped data whose developments contain trapped spheres.

papers.title: Scaling and Cross-Simulation Generalization of Graph Neural Networks for Cosmic-Web Classification in CAMELS
papers.abstract: Graph-based methods can classify galaxies by their dark-matter cosmic-web environments, but reliability beyond development simulations remains uncertain. Galaxy-formation models alter tracer populations and spatial distributions, potentially shifting graph features. We test how graph neural networks scale with independent training realizations and transfer across hydrodynamical simulations. Using the $z=0$ CAMELS IllustrisTNG, SIMBA and Astrid suites, we label galaxies with $M_\star>10^9\,M_\odot$ as void, sheet, filament or knot from the smoothed cold-dark-matter density field. We represent their spatial distributions as periodic Delaunay graphs with ten geometric descriptors. We compare a multilayer perceptron (MLP) and five graph neural networks (GNNs), including a local graph Transformer, under realization-grouped evaluation. Learning curves increase training data from 10 to 100 realizations, with validation and test boxes fixed. We test every source-to-target suite pairing on 100 unseen realizations per target suite. On this external holdout, the Transformer, GAT+ and EdgeConv reach mean per-realization macro-averaged F1 scores of $0.652$, $0.651$ and $0.642$, against $0.481$ for the MLP. The Transformer outperforms the MLP by 0.171, while the difference between the Transformer and GAT+ is not statistically significant. Voids remain the hardest class. Performance is higher in boxes with more selected galaxies and shorter Delaunay edges. Associations with cosmological and feedback parameters weaken after accounting for galaxy richness and void fraction. Our results benchmark the scaling and cross-simulation transfer of galaxy-graph classifiers, demonstrating the value of neighbourhood information and identifying tracer sampling as an important limitation for dark-matter web inference.

papers.title: Physical quasar pairs in DESI DR1 as tracers of protoclusters at $z\approx2$
papers.abstract: Close pairs of quasars at the same redshift are expected to mark overdense regions that will collapse into galaxy clusters. Earlier work with SDSS found about 2800 such pairs, too few to follow their environment with separation. We build the largest sample of physical quasar pairs to date from DESI DR1 and test whether pairs out to Mpc separations trace protoclusters. We select pairs with rest-frame velocity difference $|\Delta V|\leq900 km/s$ and projected separation $r_p\leq4$~Mpc at $1.2\leq z\leq2.8$, measure their purity and fibre completeness, and measure the clustering of pair members around all DESI quasars. We find 40\,626 physical pairs with projected separation $r_p\leq2.5$~Mpc, where their purity falls to 50\%, the effective radius of protoclusters at $z\approx2$. Pair members are $1.69\pm0.14$, $1.78\pm0.09$ and $2.01\pm0.06$ times more clustered than all quasars for projected separations $r_p\leq1$, 1--2.5 and 2.5--4~Mpc, while chance pairs show little excess ($1.08\pm0.05$). This corresponds to haloes of $\sim1.4$--$2.2\times10^{13}\,h^{-1}M_\odot$. Physical quasar pairs with projected separations up to 2.5~Mpc trace protocluster environments, at the level that AbacusSummit mocks predict in $\Lambda$CDM. The full DESI survey will turn them into a statistical census of protoclusters at cosmic noon.

The local integral quantization presented here seems to be applicable to semiclassical quantization of geodesic motion in other curved spacetimes.

papers.title: Galaxy cluster thermodynamic profiles beyond self-similarity
papers.abstract: Galaxy cluster formation is a self-similar and scale-free process of gravitational collapse. However, the thermodynamic properties of the intracluster medium often deviate from self-similar predictions. We investigate these deviations using a sample of 92 galaxy clusters selected through their Sunyaev-Zeldovich effect signal, spanning a mass range of $M_{500c}=[0.5-20] \times 10^{14}{M}_{\odot}$, and with redshifts $0.08 < z < 1.13$. Adopting a flexible framework that allows for radial variations in both redshift and mass scaling, we characterise the behaviour of scaled density, temperature, pressure, and entropy profiles, while simultaneously constraining their intrinsic scatter. We detect significant radial deviations from self-similar expectations in both redshift and mass scalings in all profiles. These deviations are strongest in the core regions, but remain measurable out to large radii ($\sim R_{500c}$), indicating that cluster outer regions are not fully described by purely gravitational evolution. We investigate the impact of an offset, a mass-dependence, and increased scatter between the mass proxy and the true mass on the radial mass scaling, finding that while its shape remains stable, its normalisation depends on the latter two effects. The pressure is the only thermodynamic quantity that exhibits approximately self-similar behaviour: outside the core it evolves self-similarly, with no dependence on mass. The entropy exhibits the strongest deviations from self-similarity as a function of radius. The intrinsic scatter peaks in the central regions and reaches a minimum at intermediate radii ($\lesssim 20 \%$ at $\sim 0.2$-$0.8 \ R_{500c}$), making this range optimal to reduce scatter in scaling relations. We conclude that the thermodynamic distributions exhibit non-self similar, mass-dependent scaling extending well beyond the core regime.

papers.title: A Genetic Algorithm Approach to Reconstructing Scalar-Tensor Lagrangians
papers.abstract: Recent DESI baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) data, combined with cosmic microwave background (CMB) and Type Ia supernovae observations, have been interpreted as evidence for dynamical dark energy whose equation of state crosses the phantom divide $w=-1$. Such a crossing cannot be realized smoothly by a minimally coupled scalar field $\varphi$, but can arise naturally in scalar-tensor theories. We present a data-driven framework that reconstructs the scalar-tensor Lagrangian directly from observations, using a genetic algorithm to evolve the symbolic expressions for the nonminimal coupling $F(\varphi)$ and the scalar potential $U(\varphi)$. Each candidate is evaluated through a forward model that self-consistently determines the expansion history, the effective gravitational coupling, and the growth of structure. Candidates are ranked by a joint likelihood of DESI DR2 BAO, Pantheon+ supernovae calibrated with SH0ES Cepheids, compressed CMB distance priors, and redshift-space distortion measurements of $f\sigma_8$. We restrict to the unscreened branch of the theory and impose Solar System constraints on the post-Newtonian parameter $\gamma$ and on the time variation of the gravitational coupling, together with a Big Bang nucleosynthesis bound on its evolution. Across 64 independent runs, the best reconstruction improves the fit relative to $\Lambda$CDM by $\Delta\chi^2=-16.6$, compared with $\Delta\chi^2=-10.6$ for the CPL dark-energy parametrization. The preferred coupling is well described by $F(\varphi)=c_1\varphi^2+e^{\varphi}(1-c_2\varphi)$. The reconstructed theory shows phantom behavior at $z\gtrsim0.5$, but it remains close to $w=-1$ at low redshift.

papers.title: Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
papers.abstract: We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrt{\Lambda}/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $\Lambda > 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $\Lambda>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

papers.title: The tangled warp of the Milky Way II: The red clump
papers.abstract: The Milky Way's disc is warped in a way that varies depending on the age of the population considered. We, for the first time, trace that kinematics of the warp in red clumps stars. This reinforces the conclusion that the Milky Way's warp is dynamically evolving, making this a necessary property of any model that seeks to explain its creation.

papers.title: Probing Dynamical Dark Energy with Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 3 Cosmic Shear
papers.abstract: Recent measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations (BAO) and Type Ia Supernovae (SNe) have revealed a preference for a time-evolving dark energy equation of state. Because such dynamical behavior alters both the cosmic expansion history and the late-time growth of structure, weak gravitational lensing measurements can be used to test these extended models. We present an extended analysis of the real-space cosmic shear two-point correlation functions (2PCFs) from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Year 3 (HSC-Y3) survey. Using over 25 million galaxies across 416 deg$^2$, divided into four tomographic redshift bins ($0.3 < z \le 1.5$), we constrain both a constant ($w$CDM) and a time-varying ($w_0w_a$CDM) dark energy equation of state. To break the geometric degeneracies inherent in cosmic shear, we combine the HSC-Y3 data with a CMB-independent suite of background distance probes: DESI DR2 BAO, the recalibrated DES five-year SN sample (DOVEKIE), and Big Bang Nucleosynthesis (BBN) priors. In the $w$CDM paradigm, our joint analysis yields $w =-0.936^{+0.074}_{-0.067}$, consistent with a cosmological constant. Within the $w_0w_a$CDM framework, we find $w_0 =-0.832^{+0.071}_{-0.059}$ and $w_a = -1.23^{+0.66}_{-0.44}$, representing a $2.4\sigma$ preference for dynamical dark energy. Although the unconstrained dark energy parameters reduce the cosmic shear-only $S_8$ constraints to smaller values, our joint multi-probe analysis agrees with the baseline HSC-Y3 $\Lambda$CDM structure growth amplitude. We obtain $S_8 = 0.774^{+0.027}_{-0.034}$ for $w$CDM and $S_8 = 0.772^{+0.031}_{-0.030}$ for $w_0w_a$CDM. Our results demonstrate that the weak lensing amplitude is robust to extended dark energy parameterizations, and that the dynamical dark energy signal is currently driven primarily by the geometric distance ladders, a critical consistency test for next-generation Stage-IV cosmological surveys.

papers.title: Signals from the early Universe: primordial features from the full-shape analysis of BOSS galaxies and eBOSS quasars in combination with Planck
papers.abstract: We search for primordial oscillatory features using cosmic microwave background (CMB) and large-scale structure (LSS) data, combining \textit{Planck} Public Release 4 (PR4) with galaxy clustering from the Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (BOSS) and quasars from the extended Baryon Oscillation Spectroscopic Survey (eBOSS). For the LSS data we perform a full-shape analysis of the power spectrum multipoles with the one-loop effective field theory of large-scale structure, applying infrared resummation separately to each oscillatory component. We consider four templates: linearly and logarithmically oscillating features in Fourier space, with constant, localised, or power-law-decaying amplitudes, and fit them to the CMB and LSS data separately and jointly. We find no statistically significant evidence for primordial features in either dataset, individually or in combination. The best-fitting LSS features improve the fit by $\Delta\chi^2\simeq-6$ to $-10$, which corresponds to global significances of at most $1.6\,\sigma$ once the look-elsewhere effect is accounted for. In the CMB alone, the most significant feature is reduced to $\sim2.6\,\sigma$. Over the full frequency range, the LSS bounds on the feature amplitudes are weaker than those from \textit{Planck} by factors of $1.4$--$3$. Combining \textit{Planck} with \textit{BOSS+eBOSS} leaves the CMB constraints essentially unchanged, because the LSS data do not favour the frequencies preferred by the CMB.

papers.title: First detection of s-cis-acroleine (sc-CH2CHCHO) in the interstellar medium
papers.abstract: We report the first interstellar detection of the higher-energy $s$-cis conformer of acrolein (CH2CHCHO) toward TMC-1 using the Quijote line survey. Local thermodynamic equilibrium modeling, assuming a rotational temperature of 7.5 K, yields a column density of $(1.0\pm0.2)\times10^{11}$~cm$^{-2}$ when fitting the observed lines. The s-cis/s-trans abundance ratio is $0.45\pm0.11$, despite an energy separation of approximately 1025~K, indicating a strongly nonequilibrium conformational distribution. An exploratory gas--grain chemical model identifies C3H5 + O as the dominant acrolein formation route, pointing to this reaction as a first entry to consider when explaining the isomeric ratios. The observed ratio provides a new constraint on conformer-specific formation, destruction, and interconversion processes in cold interstellar clouds.

papers.title: Black holes in little red and blue dots drive no superwinds in the first 1.5 billion years
papers.abstract: Galaxy-formation models rely on accreting black holes to expel gas from their hosts. We test this prediction in 67 little red dots (LRDs) and little blue dots (LBDs) in the first 1.5 billion years, selected from 80,367 NIRSpec spectra in the DAWN JWST Archive. We detect no [O III] wind, against lower limits of 7.2 and 7.5 expected detections for local sub-Eddington and super-Eddington active nuclei. For winds narrower than 1,500 km/s, the corresponding incidence limits are 13% and 19% at 95% confidence, compared with 31% and 49% locally. Broad Balmer lines are centred on the narrow lines, and Balmer absorbers move below 8% of the escape speed. Published super-Eddington fountain, black-hole-star and quasi-star models each fail a measured property of the spectra. LRDs and LBDs drive no superwinds, and their black holes grow without the wind feedback invoked to regulate galaxies.

papers.title: phenjax: the IMRPhenomT waveform family in JAX for accelerated analyses on CPUs and GPUs
papers.abstract: We present phenjax, a JAX implementation of the precessing time-domain IMRPhenomT family of models for the gravitational wave signal emitted in compact binary coalescence. The code keeps the structure of its reference Python implementation, phenomxpy, and reproduces, on average, its polarizations to a few $\times 10^{-12}$ of the peak strain for all the models, aligned-spin and precessing. The waveform models now take advantage of the JAX construction: compiled once per array shape, vectorized over events (batching), differentiable and executed on CPUs or GPUs with the same source code. Different additional features address the cost of long signals and of heterogeneous populations in a batch. On one NVIDIA H100, for the precessing TPHM model on LISA-mass populations, phenjax is 3 to 6 times faster than phenomxpy when both codes evaluate one event at a time and 20 to 30 times faster when phenjax evaluates the events in batches of 8. We estimate that, for waveform generation, one GPU does the work of 1300 to 2700 cores of a current CPU node at 25 to 45 times less energy per waveform. As a backend of a global-fit LISA massive black hole pipeline, performed on the Sangria dataset, phenjax recovers the same posteriors as the other waveform backends at a lower computational cost. In a comparison with phentax, the wall time was 13 minutes instead of 21.

papers.title: State of the UNIONS: Four Milky Way companions discovered in a systematic search for northern Local Group satellites
papers.abstract: We present four newly discovered Milky Way satellites from a systematic search through the $gri$ photometry from the Ultraviolet Near-Infrared Optical Northern Survey (UNIONS). Two of these satellites are likely ultra-faint dwarf galaxies that we have named Boötes VI and Draco III. Both galaxy candidates are $\gtrsim 100$ kpc from the Galactic center and have absolute $V$-band magnitudes ($M_V$) of $-2.7^{+0.6}_{-0.5}$ and $-4.0\pm0.6$, respectively. Boötes VI and Draco III have physical half-light radii ($r_{\rm h}$) of $\sim 50$ pc, or about twice as large as the most extended Milky Way globular clusters with similar luminosities. They are therefore candidate galaxies, though chemodynamical analyses will be needed to secure these classifications. We name the two other systems UNIONS 2 and UNIONS 3. They are extremely faint ($M_V = +0.4^{+0.6}_{-0.9}$ and $-0.7^{+0.6}_{-0.8}$) and compact ($r_{\rm h} = 5\,\pm\,1$ and $10^{+3}_{-2} pc), and zero giant stars are identified in either of their present-day stellar populations. Morphological measurements alone are not sufficient to assess the presence of dark matter in either system, so do not provide definitive classifications. We discuss the challenges in either detecting or refuting the presence of dark matter in UNIONS 2 and UNIONS 3, two systems that are archetypal of the faintest satellites that will be discovered in increasing numbers in upcoming wide-field surveys.

papers.title: The THESAN-ZOOM project: interpreting candidate Population III-enriched absorption line systems during reionization
papers.abstract: With JWST, metal absorption lines are now being detected at increasingly high redshift, where signatures of the first generation of stars (Population III) may be observable. Interpreting observations of possible Pop III-enriched gas is challenging, as metals released by stars inevitably mix with pristine gas accreting onto galaxies and recycled gas from different episodes of star formation. Inference of Pop III enrichment from low-ionisation absorption lines requires placing stellar nucleosynthesis yields within the broader context of galaxy evolution. With THESAN-ZOOM, a set of high-resolution radiation hydrodynamical zoom-in simulations of galaxies, we investigate the metal abundance patterns observable in absorption. As our fiducial simulations do not include Pop III enrichment channels, our primary goal is to test how galaxy formation processes can shape observed abundance ratios. Our results indicate that a single abundance ratio plane, such as the commonly used [Si/O] vs. [C/O], cannot conclusively distinguish Pop III enrichment from enrichment by subsequent populations of stars. Robust detections instead require characterising multiple abundance ratios. In our simulations, a larger dispersion in abundance ratio distributions (often interpreted as possible evidence of pollution from the first stellar populations) naturally arises with increasing redshift, when the metallicity and dust content are lower. However, this alone does not reproduce all the observed results. By running an additional simulation with an updated THESAN-ZOOM model containing Pop III stars, we show that this has a large impact on the simulated abundance ratios, pushing them closer to those observed in potential Pop III-enriched gas.

papers.title: Tipping the scales in Blue Jay: Dust energy balance overpredicts IR luminosity in galaxies at $z\sim2$
papers.abstract: The spectral energy distribution (SED) of a galaxy encodes vital information about its chemical composition, stellar populations, and dust content. To model the infrared emission, many modern SED-fitting codes rely on dust energy balance, which assumes that all energy absorbed by dust in the UV-optical is equal to the energy emitted by dust in the infrared regime. However, few studies have been carried out to test the validity of this assumption at high redshift, where direct infrared observations are sparse. In this work, we perform aperture photometry in 111 galaxies from the Blue Jay survey ($1.7 < z < 3.5$) using public JWST/MIRI observations from the PRIMER, COSMOS-Web and COSMOS-3D surveys. Focusing on a subsample of 89 star-forming galaxies, we reconstruct best-fit SED model spectra from Prospector using only HST and NIRCam photometry and compare the predicted mid-infrared fluxes to the measured MIRI photometry. We find that mid-infrared fluxes are systematically overpredicted by about 10% at 7.7$\mu$m up to a factor of $\sim3$ at 21$\mu$m. The discrepancy increases with inferred dust attenuation, indicating that dust energy balance suffers from line-of-sight effects in systems with complex dust geometries. We find that adding NIRSpec spectroscopy to the fits breaks parameter degeneracies and strongly reduces the overprediction. When fitting the measured MIRI photometry together with the HST and NIRCam data, the best-fit model spectra of dusty galaxies ($A_V\gtrsim1$) result in significantly lower infrared luminosities by -0.6 dex compared to best-fit spectra obtained without MIRI, consistent with steeper, SMC-like attenuation curves or complex star-dust geometries. Our study highlights the limitations of dust energy balance at high redshift and underlines the importance of direct observations for accurately recovering the ISM and dust properties of galaxies at cosmic noon.

papers.title: The Splash population confined to the Milky Way bar region
papers.abstract: We investigate the chemo-dynamical properties of in-situ stars in the Galactic bar region (central $5$ kpc), specifically the inner Galactic counterpart of the solar-neighbourhood Splash population (in situ halo). We use a sample of APOGEE DR17 red giants with Gaia astrometry and AstroNN distances, and separate bulge/bar stellar populations dynamically using a normalised time-averaged bar-frame angular momentum, $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$. Chemo-dynamical maps in the $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$-[Fe/H] plane reveal a pronounced extension of the bar population towards $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}<0$ (non-bar-following orbits) within $-1.0<{\rm [Fe/H]}<-0.3$, characterised by high eccentricities, large $z_{\rm max}$ and an extended spheroidal orbit density distribution, and accounting for $\sim 30\%$ of all stars at these metallicities. These $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}<0$ stars have [Mg/Fe] and [Al/Fe] abundances similar to those of stars on ${\rm x_1}$ orbits at the same [Fe/H], and they match the solar-neighbourhood Splash in its metallicity and abundance ratio distributions. We therefore refer to them as the $\textit{central Splash}$. The presence of a significant central Splash underscores the role of the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus merger in the early history of the Galaxy. We find a similar, weaker extension in the $\mathcal{V}_{\phi}$-[Fe/H] maps for extremely metal-rich stars, which are confined to the bulge. At metallicities [Fe/H] $<0.3$, we find no additional classical bulge population in these maps beyond the central Splash and proto-Galactic populations $-$ the high-$\alpha$ bulge appears to have evolved from the early high-$\alpha$ disc.

papers.title: A comparison of two- and one-fluid dust solvers for dusty, supersonic turbulence
papers.abstract: We model 3 and 10 $\mu$m dust grains in supersonic, turbulent molecular cloud conditions to compare two different numerical methods solving dust coupled to gas through a drag term. One method models dust and gas as two separate species (two fluid) and the other the combination of dust and gas as a single mixture (one fluid) using the diffusion approximation. Simulations are performed in a 3D periodic box using the Phantom code. The gas probability distributions are consistent with a lognormal distribution for both methods and grain sizes. The dust distributions are different in the two methods, showing discrepancies particularly in regions of low density. The most significant difference between the two methods is in the dust-to-gas ratio distributions. Both methods peak at the mean dust-to-gas ratio of 0.01, but the two-fluid method has wider distributions than the one-fluid method suggesting excess dust concentration in dense filaments. Filaments are where the one-fluid method results are most accurate. The narrowing of the one-fluid distribution is also caused by the stopping time limiter used to maintain the terminal velocity approximation. This artificially makes the mixture more coupled in low-density regions. Our overall conclusion is that both methods are viable for the study of dust in molecular clouds, but that the correct method should be chosen based on the numerical Stokes number regime of the calculation to avoid numerical artifacts.

papers.title: ACT Excited: Reconciling Starobinsky and Quadratic Chaotic Inflationary Models with ACT Results via Excited States
papers.abstract: Data Release 6 of the Atacama Cosmology Telescope, combined with Planck, CMB lensing and DESI BAO data, favours a higher scalar spectral index $n_{s}$ than Planck and a mildly positive running $\alpha_{s}$, putting the Starobinsky model in tension with the data, while the quadratic chaotic model is already excluded by its large tensor-to-scalar ratio $r$. We show that relaxing the Bunch--Davies assumption for the initial state of the scalar perturbations can restore agreement without modifying the inflaton potential. Parametrising the Bogoliubov coefficients by an excitation parameter $\chi_{S}$ and a relative phase $2\varphi_{S}$, we derive the shifts of $n_{s}$ and $\alpha_{s}$ induced by their scale dependence and map the regions of the $(\varphi_{S},\chi_{S})$ plane compatible with the $1\sigma$ ACT DR6 ranges, the bound $r<0.038$, and the requirement that the scale of new physics $\Lambda$ exceed the Hubble scale $H$. For the Starobinsky model, a scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ or $\varphi_{S}$ works almost everywhere in this plane: only small neighbourhoods of $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi$ with $\chi_{S}\gtrsim1.22$ are excluded, and a scale-dependent phase fails at $\varphi_{S}=0,\pi/2,\pi$ and at $\chi_{S}=0$, where the required ${\rm d}\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k$ and ${\rm d}^2\varphi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2$ diverge. For the QC model, the excited state must also suppress $r$, which requires $\chi_{S}\gtrsim0.63$ and $\Lambda\lesssim6H$. A scale-dependent $\chi_{S}$ must satisfy $|{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k|\gtrsim0.0021$ in both models, and in the QC model we show analytically that $0.0021\lesssim{\rm d}\chi_{S}/{\rm d}\ln k\lesssim0.0058$ and $0.0008\lesssim{\rm d}^2\chi_{S}/{\rm d}(\ln k)^2\lesssim0.0062$. If the tensor modes remain in the BD state, the scenario also predicts a violation of the consistency relation $r=-8n_{T}$, testable once the tensor power spectrum and its tilt are measured.

papers.title: A novel quantum lattice Boltzmann methodology for cosmological radiation transport
papers.abstract: Radiation transport is an essential process in many physical simulations, including cosmological codes which track stellar and diffuse radiation. Many present codes utilize ray tracing or moment methods, but these grow increasingly difficult and expensive for large simulations. Quantum lattice Boltzmann methods exponentially reduce complexity by propagating radiation over a lattice, allowing for better spatial resolution without needing to introduce adaptive ray tracing or other optimizations. However, existing formulations result in poor angular resolution for radiation point sources. In this work, we propose an angular redistribution methodology which significantly improves the resolution with minimal increase in complexity. We verify the correctness of the method on both classical processors and quantum simulators and outline how the quantum algorithm can be integrated into existing codes. This method is an important step towards fully-quantum radiation hydrodynamics simulation which could exponentially accelerate existing cosmological codes, enabling simulations at scales currently infeasible.

papers.title: Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology
papers.abstract: We propose a new framework for inhomogeneous cosmology based on General Relativity sourced by an anisotropic fluid. The model is parametrized by a single input function, the radial Misner--Sharp mass distribution at different redshifts, and admits exact solutions to Einstein's equations. Going beyond the standard assumption of small metric perturbations, it provides a fully relativistic framework to describe the non-linear regime of cosmic structure formation. The Friedmann-Lemaître-Robertson-Walker (FLRW) cosmology is recovered both at early times and -- on large scales only -- at late times. Our Anisotropic Fluid Inhomogeneous Cosmology (AFIC) model provides a natural mechanism through which matter inhomogeneities give rise to late-time acceleration. The extensive term driving this effect does not enter the exact metric solution and therefore does not contribute to the local gravitational potential. Rather, it emerges as a genuinely large-scale effect induced by the inhomogeneous distribution of matter at late times. This mechanism may provide a physical interpretation of the results from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI). Finally, we present a simple analytical realization of the model and use it to provide an estimate of the present-day effective dark energy density.

papers.title: RIFT for the O4 era: operating points, calibration marginalization, and cross-code validation
papers.abstract: The Rapid Iterative FiTting (RIFT) parameter inference algorithm provides a simulation-based-inference approach to efficient, highly-parallelized parameter inference for GW sources. In this paper, we describe improvements deployed during preparations for and analysis of O4 observations (versions this http URL--this http URL) that broaden RIFT's reach for single-event inference with contemporary instruments. We provide additional options to increase compatibility and comparability with other codes, notably including (a) enhancing RIFT's capabilities for calibration marginalization; (b) managing our likelihood's internal, output, and time-interpolated representation; (c) introducing new coordinates for (transverse) spin and eccentric mean anomaly, enabling more robust inference of parameters with subtle and complex correlations to others, and (d) revised operating point choices better suited to the loudest, clearest signals. We identify and reconcile the most substantial sources of head-to-head likelihood differences between RIFT and other production inference codes, and describe automated waveform symmetry checks that detect upstream model regressions before they bias inference. Using the previously-reported RIFT/asimov interface for reproducible settings consistent with past work, we demonstrate these capabilities end to end.
