papers.title: Unitarity with respect to the Clock of a Dynamical Local Observer and the Einstein Equivalence Principle
papers.abstract: We investigate the unitarity of quantum evolution with respect to an internal time defined by a local observer's clock. The observer is modeled as a relativistic particle carrying both a clock and a matter-field detector, analyzed first on a fixed curved background and subsequently within a fully diffeomorphism-invariant theory of dynamical gravity. In the former case, we find that evolution relative to the internal clock is generally nonunitary, implying a violation of the Einstein equivalence principle at the quantum level. In contrast, in the latter case, diffeomorphism invariance allows us to adopt observer-centric coordinates. On the resulting partially reduced phase space, one of the diffeomorphism generators becomes linear in the clock Hamiltonian, generating a relational evolution that is consistent with the remaining diffeomorphism constraints. Assuming the existence of an effective quantum theory that consistently preserves diffeomorphism invariance, these features imply unitary evolution relative to the internal clock, thereby preserving the equivalence principle even in the quantum regime. Our results highlight the fundamental role of diffeomorphism invariance in shaping relational unitary evolution from the perspective of a local observer.
papers.comments: 34 pages, 3 figures. Accepted for publication in Physical Review D. Title changed; conclusions unchanged

papers.title: Carroll limits of bosonic and supersymmetric D-branes in the Polyakov formulation
papers.abstract: We derive the magnetic and electric Carroll limits of bosonic and supersymmetric D-branes in the Polyakov formulation at fixed positive rescaled tension. Eliminating the nonsymmetric auxiliary tensor recovers the full Dirac--Born--Infeld action. On the regular domain with a positive-definite induced spatial metric and a positive lapse bounded away from zero, the auxiliary constraints remain second class in both limits. Eliminating them before or after contraction gives the same local reduced phase space. The magnetic Hamiltonian retains the full spatial determinant and the electric Hamiltonian retains the electric displacement squared. We compare their dynamics on flat D2 solutions and on curves in a common warped Carroll background. Both limits retain sixteen independent $\kappa$-symmetry parameters for flat Type II D2--D7 branes. The electric limit also retains a Neveu--Schwarz flux term in the fermionic constraint and supercharge matrices. Spatial T-duality commutes with both contractions on fixed-radius circle zero modes when the dual transverse canonical pair is rescaled in the electric case. The prescribed local Carroll--Weyl transformation fails to preserve the constraints, and both actions admit exact global dilations.

papers.title: A catalogue of insights from the fourth LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA observing run
papers.abstract: Over the last decade, gravitational-wave science has developed from a detection being a Nobel-winning achievement to an (almost) everyday occurrence. The LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) Collaboration's flagship scientific results are now their catalogues of detections. We review discoveries from the fourth observing run (O4) of the \ac{LVK}. The recent catalogues each include $\sim100$ new detections. Among these are remarkable single discoveries: the loudest signals detected, and sources unlike those seen before. However, significant advances also are coming from population-level analyses, leveraging the sample size to infer constraints on the astrophysical distribution of merging compact binaries, potential deviations from general relativity, and the expansion rate of the Universe. Analyses of the latest data have revealed evidence for multiple subpopulations of sources, providing a unique probe into the evolution of coalescing binaries. Our understanding of gravitational-wave signals and their sources will continue to deepen with more observations: the final catalogue from O4 will release in December 2026, and planned future observing runs with greater detector sensitivity will bring even larger catalogues and additional loud signals.
papers.comments: 19 pages (1 page title+abstract, 9 pages main text, 9 pages bibliography), 4 figures; updated to match published version, with additional citations beyond journal limit

papers.title: Interstellar Complex Organic Molecules and Molecular Outflows in NGC 1333 IRAS 4B and 4B' Observed Using NOEMA
papers.abstract: We present interferometric observations with the Northern Extended Millimeter Array (NOEMA) of NGC 1333 IRAS 4B and 4B', two young stellar objects (YSOs) within the Perseus molecular cloud. YSOs, especially Class 0 protostars, are rich in gas-phase interstellar complex organic molecules (iCOMs), but relatively little is known about the spatial distribution of these important prebiotic molecules. Various molecules were imaged within IRAS 4B and the surrounding area in the 145 GHz spectral range, revealing hundreds of molecular transitions within the warm inner envelope of IRAS 4B. This work provides derived physical parameters (rotational temperature, column density, velocity shift with respect to local standard of rest, and full-width at half-maximum spectral line width) for 11 molecules toward IRAS 4B including methanol (CH$_3$OH and isotopologues), methyl formate (HCOOCH$_3$), dimethyl ether (CH$_3$OCH$_3$), acetaldehyde (CH$_3$CHO), ethanol (C$_2$H$_5$OH), glycolaldehyde (CH$_2$OHCHO), acetone (CH$_3$COCH$_3$), and isocyanic acid (HNCO). Out of these molecules, 10 are iCOMs (excluding HNCO) that trace the inner envelope of IRAS 4B and mark it as a rich source of organic material. There is a strong spatial correlation between the continuum emission of IRAS 4B and iCOM molecular emission and among various iCOMs with each other. Physical parameter and integrated intensity maps show that IRAS 4B is a binary protostar system that drives a jet in a north-south orientation and an outflow in a northwest-southeast orientation. IRAS 4B' also drives a west-east outflow but shows no evidence of molecular emission cospatial with its continuum emission.

papers.title: Radiation Magneto-hydrodynamic Simulations of MRI with Zero-Net-Vertical-Flux: Necessity of Resolving the Thermal Scale For Strongly Magnetized Initial Conditions
papers.abstract: We perform 3D radiation magneto-hydrodynamic (RMHD) shearing-box simulations of local patches of optically thick accretion disks, applicable to sub-Eddington active galactic nuclei (AGN) at $\sim 1000$ gravitational radii around a supermassive black hole (SMBH) of $10^7-10^8M_\odot$. In particular, we set up zero-net-vertical-flux (ZNVF) simulations with strong net azimuthal fields ($B_y$) characterized by initial gas-to-magnetic pressure ratio $\beta_0$. We find that $\beta_0 \sim 1$ simulations relax to the classical MRI state with steady-state $\beta\sim 10-20$ and slow periodic reversals of the mean azimuthal field (dynamo cycles), losing memory of their initial $B_y$ configuration. The outcome of simulations starting from $\beta_0=0.1$ (superthermal magnetic pressures) depends upon the numerical resolution as quantified by the number of grid cells per thermal scale height $H_\mathrm{th}$. Resolved simulations ($\Delta z\le H_\mathrm{th}/5$) settle into final states similar to the larger-$\beta_0$ runs, exhibiting thermally dominated midplanes heated by MRI turbulence and undergoing dynamo cycles. In contrast, lower resolution $\beta_0 = 0.1$ runs evolve towards states dominated by a coherent mean field, similar to what is observed in recent isothermal MHD simulations. However, those disks fail to sustain sufficient turbulent heating near the midplane and undergo runaway cooling and contraction. While such states might be sustained in global models with even lower initial $\beta_0$ and/or continuous $B_y$ injection, our results indicate that they could arise purely from under-resolving the midplane MRI dynamo that would otherwise be able to generate and emanate randomized fields. We highlight the need to resolve a fraction of the thermal scale height (the classical MRI wavelengths) for strongly magnetized initial conditions to obtain converged outcomes in RMHD simulations.

papers.title: StAGE: Stellar Archaeology-driven Galaxy Evolution II. Binary Black Hole Mergers in Quiescent Galaxies and their Star-forming Progenitors
papers.abstract: We apply StAGE, a data-driven galaxy-evolution framework based on stellar archaeology, to study binary black hole (BBH) mergers associated with present-day quiescent galaxies (QGs) and their star-forming progenitors. By combining StAGE star-formation and chemical-enrichment histories with pre-computed SEVN population-synthesis catalogs, we predict the BBH merger-rate density, intrinsic binary properties, merger-time host-galaxy distributions, and the associated stochastic gravitational-wave (GW) background. A distinctive feature of StAGE is that it jointly tracks the stellar-binary environment at birth and the properties of the host galaxy at merger time. Moreover, stellar-archaeology constraints on $\alpha$-enhancement allow us to explore how adopting the iron abundance relevant for massive-star winds, rather than oxygen-based total metallicity, affects the predicted BBH merger rates. We find that most BBHs form at moderately subsolar metallicities $Z\lesssim Z_\odot/3$, while their merger-time hosts typically have stellar masses $M_\star\sim10^{10}-10^{11.5}\,M_\odot$ at $z\lesssim2$. At and beyond cosmic noon, hosts lie mainly on the star-forming main sequence, whereas starbursting and quenching descendants contribute increasingly toward lower redshift. Using the independent approach offered by StAGE, we also confirm recent literature findings that, for most binary-evolution prescriptions, predicted local BBH merger rates exceed the LVK-inferred range, while dynamical formation in stellar clusters extends the BBH primary mass distribution into the high-mass regime poorly populated by isolated binaries. Finally, the predicted stochastic background approaches the projected sensitivity of planned LVK upgrades and lies within reach of the Einstein Telescope. All in all, StAGE can provide physically motivated host priors for GW-source localization and dark-siren cosmology.
papers.comments: 57 pages, 19 figures. Accepted for publication in JCAP

papers.title: Two-dimensional weak lensing shear for cluster mass, concentration, ellipticity and miscentering estimation
papers.abstract: The effects of weak gravitational lensing induced by clusters of galaxies makes it possible to constrain their dark matter distribution. In general mass estimates from weak lensing are made by compressing the two-dimensional shear-field into one-dimension. In this work we build a forward model of the two-dimensional reduced-shear field around a galaxy cluster, including the non-Gaussian correlated large-scale structure from N-body simulations, the uncorrelated line-of-sight structure, cluster miscentering and ellipticity. We then use simulation-based inference to obtain posteriors on the cluster mass, concentration, miscentering and ellipticity from the full field. The two-dimensional approach leads to improvements on cluster mass constraints by up to 20\%. We show that this is due to a better treatment of the spatially correlated noise across the shear field. There is also significant improvements on the cluster concentration and miscentering. Whilst improvements are also made to the estimation of cluster ellipticity, the constraints are still prior dependent for these individual cluster constraints. We also quantify the impact of the line-of-sight structure on the constraints. Neglecting it underestimates the mass uncertainty by up to a factor of $2$ for the most massive clusters.

papers.title: MUSE spectroscopy of the compact dual AGN in the $z=3.273$ radio-loud gravitational lens MG B2016+112
papers.abstract: Dual active galactic nuclei (AGN) are unique laboratories for studying how galaxy mergers trigger accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs). However, only a few dual AGN with projected separations $\lesssim$ 1 kpc at redshifts $z>1$ have been confirmed to date. We present archival MUSE spectroscopy of the three resolved lensed images of the radio-loud type-II system MG B2016+this http URL $z=3.273$ and at a projected separation of 175 pc, this is the most compact confirmed dual AGN at $z > 1$. We detect Ly$\alpha$, C IV, N V, He II, and C III] emission across images A--C after correcting for ISM absorption at $z \sim 0$. We find that the Ly$\alpha$, C IV, and N V lines are affected by saturated absorption at $z\sim 3.27$. The He II / C III] emission-line ratios are consistent between images A and B but differ significantly from image C. We fit the Ly$\alpha$ and C IV emission regions in images A--C with a broad and a narrow Gaussian and use the broad Gaussian components in C IV to place lower limits on their respective SMBH masses: $\gtrsim 5.5 \times {10}^{6} M_\odot$, $\gtrsim 6.3 \times {10}^{6} M_\odot$, and $\gtrsim 4.8 \times {10}^{6} M_\odot$. We then combine these SMBH mass limits with the magnification-corrected luminosities derived from both the MUSE data and recent Chandra X-ray observations to estimate their Eddington ratios. Our findings motivate deep, spatially resolved near-IR spectroscopy to independently determine the SMBH masses from H$\alpha$ and H$\beta$ emission and determine the physical conditions of the host galaxy.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 4 figures, 2 tables. Accepted for publication in ApJL on 16 November 2026. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: Exact algebraic separation of the gravitoelectromagnetic perturbations of Kerr-Newman-(anti-)de Sitter black holes
papers.abstract: We obtain an explicit separation of the coupled gravitational and electromagnetic radiative equations on nonextremal Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter black holes with nonzero charge and rotation. By directly matching the Fourier coefficients, we construct a separating matrix with constant determinant that is independent of the frequency and azimuthal number and applies to both spin sectors. We establish that this transformation is smooth and invertible throughout the open AdS exterior and between the event and cosmological horizons in dS. The resulting radial and angular systems are valid at arbitrary complex frequencies. We also translate the regularity of the radiative Newman--Penrose variables at the rotation axes and future horizons into boundary conditions for the separated solutions. In the asymptotically flat limit, the transformation is related to Hintz's matrix integrating factor by the allowed frame freedom. These results provide a basis for studying quasinormal modes and black hole stability in Kerr--Newman--(anti-)de Sitter spacetimes, as well as exploring holographic applications to strongly coupled systems.

papers.title: Targeting the future of spectroscopic galaxy surveys -- A cosmological study case with the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope
papers.abstract: The next generation of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys are designed to measure hundreds of millions of galaxy and quasar spectra, extending precision large-scale-structure cosmology to redshifts and volumes well beyond the reach of current Stage-IV facilities. Realising this potential requires revisiting the target selection strategies and designing them explicitly around the depth, multiplexing, and survey time of the new instruments, rather than a direct extrapolation of existing recipes. This work develops and characterises new strategies for the Wide-field Spectroscopic Telescope (WST), a proposed 12-metre, highly multiplexed facility expected to operate in the 2040s. Using deep multi-band photometry, including COSMOS-field data from CLAUDS and HSC, we revisit low-redshift $z \lesssim 1.6$ tracer selection of SDSS, BOSS/eBOSS, DESI and 4MOST-CRS -- Bright Galaxies, Luminous Red Galaxies, Emission Line Galaxies and quasars -- to photometric depth achievable in the WST era, and introduce a purely magnitude-limited sample (MagMax) exploiting three-dimensional color-color star-galaxy separation, and a set of Lyman-Break Galaxy dropout samples extending target selection to $z \gtrsim 2$. Using Fisher-matrix forecasts, we showcase the constraining power of a WST-like cosmological survey on BAO distance parameters $\alpha_\parallel$ and $\alpha_\perp$, the growth rate $f$, the evolving dark energy equation $w_0w_a$, the local-type primordial non-Gaussianity $f_{\rm NL}^{\rm loc}$, and the sum of the neutrino mass $\Sigma m_\nu$. The main outcome of this work is an optimisation framework that directly links instrumental capabilities and observing time to cosmological constraining power, providing a science-driven template applicable to the design of future generations of Stage-V spectroscopic surveys.

papers.title: A new toric ALF gravitational instanton
papers.abstract: We construct a new explicit toric ALF gravitational instanton. The instanton has Euler characteristic $\chi = 4$ and Hirzebruch signature $\tau = -1$. The topology at infinity is a lens space $L(3,1)$. The solution depends on one parameter and is constructed from the Belinski--Zakharov four-soliton solution. We prove that the instanton is smooth and positive definite on and away from the axis. This is the first example of a non-Hermitian ALF (not AF) gravitational instanton.
papers.comments: 8 pages. v2: Fixed orientation consistency issues and typos

papers.title: The out-state of scalar-induced gravitational waves
papers.abstract: Scalar-induced second-order tensor perturbations comprise both a forced response and freely propagating gravitational waves, the radiative signal sought in observations. We define this free radiation as the out-state, whose amplitudes are given by the light-cone residue of the kernel for each scalar pair via a classical LSZ-type reduction formula. We prove a classical equivalence theorem: tensor redefinitions whose shifts have power-law envelopes and no tensor-frequency component leave the out-state invariant. For any constant equation of state $0<w<1$, the out-state is consequently universal across all intrinsic gauges, in which the slicing and spatial coordinates are fixed locally by matter and geometry without an external clock. This class includes the comoving and uniform-density gauges, whose spectra grow without bound at late times in radiation domination. Over this range of $w$, the late-time Newtonian-gauge kernel yields the out-state, justifying its standard use in computing the gravitational-wave energy spectrum. In matter domination, by contrast, the out-state isolates the free wave from the static tidal response that asymptotically dominates the Newtonian-gauge tensor perturbation.

papers.title: HydróDex: gotta match 'em all!
papers.abstract: First-order phase transitions can source a stochastic gravitational-wave background within reach of LISA and other future detectors, with sound waves in the plasma typically providing the dominant contribution. Predicting the resulting gravitational-wave signal requires determining the stationary fluid profiles around expanding bubbles. We present a complete hydrodynamic classification of these profiles in the constant-sound-speed model, which generalizes the bag model by allowing the sound speeds in front of and behind the wall, $c_+$ and $c_-$, to differ. Solving the matching conditions at the wall and evolving the surrounding plasma, we recover the known direct and inverse detonations, deflagrations, and hybrids, and uncover mixed hybrids, a new class with rarefaction waves on both sides of the wall and oppositely directed fluid flows. For a sufficiently pronounced hierarchy $c_+>c_-$, multiple stationary profiles can correspond to the same wall velocity $\xi_w$ and asymptotic transition strength $\alpha_N$. This non-uniqueness arises because this parametrization discards thermodynamic information and is resolved once the underlying microphysics is specified. We compute the kinetic-energy budget and acoustic gravitational-wave spectra within the sound-shell model, finding that mixed hybrids introduce no additional spectral feature and can be mimicked by ordinary direct or inverse hybrids with substantially different fluid profiles. Finally, we release HydróDex, a public code implementing the complete classification, profile construction, energy-budget calculation, and gravitational-wave prediction.

papers.title: Fluid/Gravity Correspondence in 3d Flat Gravity with Non-Compact Boundaries
papers.abstract: We study 3d flat gravity on a restricted phase space with a non-compact spatial boundary. The charge algebra splits into two commuting chiral current algebras, which a fluid/gravity dictionary maps to the stress tensor of a two-dimensional conformal fluid, with energy bounded below by the momentum. On the line, finiteness of the charges selects integrable, square-integrable currents, and the global data are carried by the scattering variables of a Schrödinger operator rather than by a monodromy. We analyze Heisenberg-like and Dirichlet-like boundary conditions; the latter give independently propagating chiral kinks associated with the reflectionless Pöschl-Teller operator. Both admit first-law relations. We outline the quantization as a Weyl $C^*$-algebra with quasi-free states. Retaining the radial dependence, the quasi-local stress tensor obeys an exact, non-perturbative flow of square-root $T\bar T$ type, which integrates to a finite boost in the radial position.
papers.comments: Minor changes, typos corrected and references added

papers.title: Towards modelling redshift uncertainties in the photometric void size function
papers.abstract: We present an extension of the theoretical formalism for the Void Size Function (VSF) to incorporate photometric redshift uncertainties, combining the excursion set with the theory of Lagrangian density peaks. Photometric redshift scatter induces anisotropic line-of-sight smoothing of the density field, which modifies the variance of the field and suppresses the abundance of large voids. We model this effect by damping the variance of the smoothed density field in the theoretical model, and we test it on AbacusSummit halo lightcones with true redshifts and with mock photometric redshifts generated with a Gaussian scatter. The predicted damping of the variance agrees with the one measured in the halo distribution to 1% and the suppression of the VSF due to photometric redshift scatter is well reproduced by the modified model, with recalibrated barrier parameters, for sigma_z <= 0.015 and for voids larger than 40 Mpc/h (about 2.5 mean tracer separations). This work is a first step towards modelling the VSF in modern photometric surveys such as the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Legacy Survey of Space and Time and the Euclid mission.
papers.comments: 13 pages, 3 figures, 2 tables. Prepared for submission to ApJL

papers.title: The Generalized Second Law from Fluctuation Theorems in a Quantum Reference Frame
papers.abstract: We prove the generalized second law (GSL) for black-hole exteriors undergoing unitary driving and relaxation on a fixed semifinite algebra. Wall's influential proof [arXiv:1105.3445] assumes semiclassical geometry and restricts fixed parent states to algebras of successive horizon cuts. We instead evolve the state on a fixed dressed exterior algebra. With complete characteristic data, the same semiclassical exterior supports both descriptions, analogous to the Heisenberg and Schrödinger pictures through state-operator duality. The asymptotic horizon charge is the momentum of a quantum clock; its conjugate gives the reading. The modular crossed product admits density operators whose entropy with respect to its trace reproduces generalized entropy up to clock contributions. Our approach parallels thermodynamics in regulated field theory and formulates the GSL through a quantum channel fluctuation theorem (FT) for the open exterior. We develop three complementary formulations under specified dynamical assumptions. Separated unitary driving and relaxation combine modular work, the physical-process first law relating horizon absorption to area gain, and relative-entropy contraction through data processing. A time-local description accommodates simultaneous unitary driving and dissipation. A two-time measurement of surprisal, the negative logarithm of the density operator, gives an FT for the complete exterior channel. It identifies the correction for a nonunital channel and gives a GSL bound for unital evolution without resolving intermediate dynamics. Relaxation that preserves every dressed-charge sector and the full faithful dressed reference state is unital. Unitality is sufficient for this FT proof but is not necessary for the GSL along a particular evolution. The bounds establish the GSL in the slow-clock limit when the errors vanish and quantify what is needed at finite clock width.

papers.title: The Simons Observatory: Analysis of methods for polarization calibration of multiple instruments
papers.abstract: Cosmic birefringence, the rotation of the CMB linear polarization plane across the Universe, is a powerful test of parity-violating physics beyond the Standard Model. Static isotropic rotation, however, is limited by an instrument's absolute polarization-angle calibration. We present a method for transferring absolute calibration between Simons Observatory (SO) instruments, validated on map-level simulations of the Large Aperture Telescope (LAT) and Small Aperture Telescopes (SATs) with lensed CMB polarization, polarized Galactic foregrounds, correlated instrumental noise, and polarization-angle miscalibration. We develop two pipelines: a joint LAT+SAT likelihood transferring calibration through their overlap, and the Minami-Komatsu foreground-based method, which separates cosmic birefringence from instrumental miscalibration using Galactic dust polarization without an external angle prior. We derive a general variance budget showing that calibration transfer improves sensitivity only when the combined reference and overlap transfer uncertainties remain below the receiving instrument's calibration uncertainty. While transfer does not lower the absolute-angle floor for isotropic $\beta$, it anchors the receiving instrument's multipole range. The relative-angle uncertainty is $\sim 0.1^\circ$ for $\ell_{\max}^{\mathrm{SAT}}=300$, improving to $\sim 0.04^\circ$ at $\ell_{\max}^{\mathrm{SAT}}=600$, subject to SAT beam and transfer-function control. Finally, for $\beta=0.3^\circ$, we show how the LAT's $\ell$-range distinguishes scale-independent dark-energy rotation from scale-dependent axion dark-matter models via $C_\ell^{EB}$.
